title: No funding for Pax Silica in BCDA's proposed 2027 budget
summary: The Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) on Wednesday confirmed that there was no allocation for the proposed Pax Silica initiative under its proposed P1.14 billion national government…

blocks.text: The Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) on Wednesday confirmed that there was no allocation for the proposed Pax Silica initiative under its proposed P1.14 billion national government subsidy for fiscal year 2027.

Senator Bam Aquino, budget sponsor for BCDA, said this during the plenary deliberations when asked by Senator Imee Marcos about the allocation for Pax Silica under the proposed 2027 budget of the agency.
“There is none, Mr. President,” Aquino said.

Marcos pressed if the budget sponsor was categorically confirming that there was no allocation for Pax Silica under BCDA’s corporate operating budget for 2026 and 2027, including its internally generated funds.
“There is none. I'm confirming with our new President, Ariel Nepomuceno,” Aquino answered.
“There is no funding for Pax Silica in the GAA or with [BCDA’s] internally generated budget. So there is none,” he added.
Marcos then asked if there was any allocation for the compensation and relocation of residents expected to be displaced by the project.
Aquino said that P322 million in financial assistance was allocated, but clarified that the amount was not particularly for those affected by Pax Silica, but for all BCDA areas.
“But, if ever there would be assistance to the families there, it would be coming from this budget. It is not in the committee report; it is in their corporate funds,” he said.
During the plenary deliberations, the BCDA likewise committed to hold off on any possible displacement of residents due to the Pax Silica initiative, pending sufficient funds.

This came after Marcos asked who would be shouldering the cost that will be incurred by the transfer of those who will be possibly displaced, their relocation, and the restitution of their livelihoods if there was no corresponding budgetary allocation for Pax Silica.
“There’s a commitment that BCDA will be handling all of these concerns, while the locators will be funding the actual physical development of the area,” Aquino said.

Marcos clarified whether this means that the BCDA is committing that no resident will be displaced, no agricultural land will be cleared, and no community will be relocated until enough funds are secured and their rights are acknowledged and respected.
“Yes, there's a commitment, Mr. President, from BCDA,” Aquino answered. —AOL, GMA News
